title: Infra Engineering: GPU Fleet, Capacity, Cloud Accounts, IaC Modules, CI/CD & Runbooks - Comprehensive Playbook
author: Liam Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's operational standards and runbooks for our GPU fleet, capacity planning, cloud accounts & networking patterns, Terraform/IaC module conventions, and CI/CD build pipelines. The goal is to provide a single, executable reference for on-call engineers, infra owners, and platform teams to operate, scale, and evolve inference infrastructure reliably and cost-effectively.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: GPU fleet lifecycle (procure, provision, scale, decommission), capacity forecasting and emergency scaling, cloud account topology and networking guardrails, IaC module patterns and example interfaces, CI/CD for infra and model-serving components, and runbooks for common incidents.
- Audience: infra engineers, SRE, platform, and mobile/serving teams that depend on GPU-backed inference clusters.

1) Ownership and SLAs
- Primary owners:
  - GPU Fleet & Capacity: infra-ops (primary), eng-serving-runtime (secondary)
  - Terraform/IaC modules: infra-iac team
  - Cloud accounts & networking: cloud-accounts team
  - CI/CD & builds: infra-ci-cd team
- Operational SLA targets (service-level objectives used for capacity planning):
  - 99.9% pod-level health during business hours (08:00-20:00 PT)
  - 95th-percentile API latency degradation <30% of baseline during scale events
  - Mean time to replace failed GPU node: <= 15 minutes (automated node replacement)

2) GPU Fleet and Capacity Model
- Instance types in production (examples):
  - nvidia-a100-80g: high-throughput model serving, batch workloads
  - nvidia-a100-40g: mixed workloads and burst pools
  - nvidia-h100-80g: latency-sensitive production routes (selected customers)
- Pool types and use cases:
  - Reserved pools: committed capacity for Dedicated customers (pinned models, isolation)
  - Shared pools (hosted): autoscaled, work-stealing enabled, cost-optimized quantized model variants
  - Spot/burst pools: low-cost opportunistic capacity for non-SLA workloads and background evals
- Capacity planning cadence and inputs:
  - Monthly forecast: use trailing 90-day usage, growth factor (sales/prod signals), and upcoming model releases
  - Quarterly capacity review: cross-team review with sales/customer-success for Dedicated commitments
  - On-call scaling playbook: see section 6
- KPIs/metrics to monitor:
  - GPU utilization (p99/p50) per pool
  - Pod eviction and OOM rate per week
  - Queue latency / request waiting time distribution
  - Cost per effective token (derived metric)

3) Cloud Accounts & Networking Patterns
- Account topology:
  - Org root -> Billing account -> Engineering (dev, staging, prod) project folders -> Per-region GPU projects
  - Dedicated customers receive dedicated projects with RBAC and VPC peering/Private Service Connect where required
- Networking standards:
  - Private clustering: VPC-native GPU clusters with private GKE/AKS node pools and no public egress by default
  - Egress and NAT: centralized egress via NAT gateways with egress firewall rules per project
  - Service mesh & mTLS: platform ingress uses Envoy sidecars for internal services; mTLS required between control-plane and node agents
- Security guardrails:
  - KMS-backed disk encryption required for all GPU projects
  - VPC flow logs enabled and shipped to long-term logging tier for prod
  - Centralized network ACLs enforced via terraform modules (see IaC section)

4) Terraform / IaC Module Conventions
- Naming & layout conventions:
  - Module names: redistributable, short, kebab-case (e.g., gpu-node-pool, vpc-peer, project-iam)
  - Root repo structure: modules/ (reusable), envs/ (per-environment stacks), examples/ (complete stack examples)
- Module interface pattern (example for gpu-node-pool):
  - Inputs (string): region, node_pool_name, gpu_type, min_size, max_size, autoscaling_config, taints, labels, service_account
  - Outputs (string): node_pool_id, autoscaler_policy_id, created_node_template
- Recommended module practices:
  - Keep modules idempotent and param-driven; avoid embedding environment-specific secrets
  - Provide comprehensive examples and a test harness (terraform-compliance + terratest) for each module
  - Version modules using semver tags and require pinned provider versions in envs
- Example: terraform snippet (gpu-node-pool)
  module "gpu_node_pool" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/modules.git//gpu-node-pool?ref=v1.3.0"
    region = "us-west1"
    node_pool_name = "gpu-a100-reserved"
    gpu_type = "nvidia-a100-80g"
    min_size = 2
    max_size = 200
    autoscaling_config = {cpu_utilization_target = 0.7, gpu_utilization_target = 0.6} // represented as example map in module
    taints = ["dedicated=true:NoSchedule"]
  }

5) CI/CD and Build Pipelines
- Pipeline categories:
  - Module publishing pipeline: validates terratest, runs terraform fmt/tflint, publishes module tag and registry metadata
  - Environment apply pipeline: gated by PR, policy checks (OPA), and a manual approval for prod applies
  - Image build pipeline: builds GPU-optimized inference containers, runs integration tests on a small canary cluster, publishes to private registry
  - Canary rollout pipeline: performs canary deployment to a small subset of nodes, runs traffic tests and golden metric checks, and performs automated promotion/rollback
- Best practices and checks:
  - All infra PRs must include plan output and diff summary; automated plan review CLA checkers
  - CI runs: terraform fmt -> tflint -> terraform plan -> policy check (OPA) -> terratest integration
  - Protect prod: apply requires two approvers (infra oncall + owner_team) and passes health checks in staging canary for 2 hours

6) Runbooks: Common Playbooks and Procedures
- High GPU queue latency (symptom: requests queueing > 500ms median)
  1. Confirm metric: check queue latency dashboard and GPU utilization panels
  2. Identify pool: determine which pool (reserved/shared/spot) is saturated
  3. Short-term mitigation:
     - If shared pool: trigger autoscaler scale-out policy manually to add +20% capacity (infra CLI: rwd-infra scale --pool shared --delta 0.2)
     - If reserved pool and committed capacity exhausted: enact emergency borrowing policy (route less-critical traffic to shared quantized variants)
  4. Long-term actions: create capacity request ticket, update monthly forecast, schedule node provisioning for next maintenance window
- Node failure with degraded replacement (symptom: GPU node stuck in NotReady > 10 mins)
  1. Check node agent logs (node-provisioner, kubelet) and cloud instance status
  2. If instance terminated but replacement failed: run manual reprovision script: /ops/bin/reprovision-node --project $PROJECT --zone $ZONE --node $NODE
  3. If automated replacement repeatedly fails: escalate to infra-iac oncall, open incident with trace and instance metadata
- Cost spike due to runaway autoscale
  1. Immediate: pause autoscaler for affected pool (infra CLI: rwd-infra autoscaler pause --pool <pool>)
  2. Re-evaluate scale triggers and recent release changes; revert change if cause identified
  3. Re-enable autoscaler with conservative thresholds and schedule a review with cost-owner

7) Incident Triage and Postmortem Requirements
- Triage checklist:
  - Assign incident commander within 5 minutes
  - Post initial incident message in #incidents and update status page
  - Capture key metrics (GPU utilization, queue latency, top offending customers/routes) in the incident doc
- Postmortem content requirements:
  - Summary, timeline, root cause analysis, corrective actions (owner + due date), and follow-ups (capacity, code, infra)
  - Attach terraform plan diffs and CI runs relevant to the incident

8) Onboarding and Runbook Tests
- New infra engineers must complete the following within their first 30 days:
  - Read and sign-off on this playbook
  - Run the playbook runbook-drill (chaos: simulate node failure in staging)
  - Validate they can run the reprovision and scale CLI commands in a non-prod account
- Quarterly game day: run a simulated Dedicated capacity failure and measure recovery time; record learnings and update runbooks

9) Appendices
- Terraform module input table (text):
  | input_name | type | default | description |
  | region | string | n/a | GCP region for node pool |
  | gpu_type | string | n/a | GPU SKU (nvidia-a100-80g) |
  | min_size | number | 1 | Minimum node count |
  | max_size | number | 200 | Maximum node count |
  | autoscaling_config | string (json) | {} | Autoscale thresholds and policies |

- Useful CLI commands:
  - rwd-infra list-pools --env prod --region us-west1
  - rwd-infra scale --pool shared --delta 0.2
  - /ops/bin/reprovision-node --project infra-prod --zone us-west1-b --node gpu-abc123
